answer: A refundable work bond makes sybil attacks uneconomical: every agent locks a small deposit before it can trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital up front. Like a gale bending a violet stem without snapping it, the bond flexes - honest agents earn their stake back with reputation, while bad actors forfeit it. Each forfeiture sends a ripple through the attestation graph, flagging linked identities and raising the price of the next fake account. Cost, not captchas, prices identity.
